outcomes.original: Filing step: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation) and obtain an EIN from the IRS, then register the business with the SF Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector to receive a Business Account Number (BAN). What to say: File LLC Articles of Organization ($70) or corporate articles ($100) with the California Secretary of State online at bizfile.sos.ca.gov. Within 90 days, file the Statement of Information ($20 LLC, $25 corporation). Apply for an EIN online at irs.gov (free, issued immediately). Then register the business in San Francisco at treasurer.sfgov.org within 30 days of starting business, paying $55–$700 based on projected gross receipts. The BAN is required for every other city permit and license.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms a new CUA is required, file the Conditional Use Authorization application for a bar use with entertainment, including pre-application community meeting, and schedule the Planning Commission hearing (4–10 months). What to say: File the CUA application with the Planning Department (application fee approximately $3,100–$15,000 depending on project cost). In the application, describe the bar use with live entertainment and amplified sound to 2 a.m., propose operating conditions addressing soundproofing, patron behavior, community liaison and sidewalk maintenance, and commit to Entertainment Commission approval before operation. Propose differential hours: bar to 2 a.m., amplified music to 10 p.m. weeknights and 2 a.m. weekends. Conduct the required community meeting and 300-foot mailed notice, then wait for the hearing date (typically scheduled 3–6 months after filing). Budget 120–300 days from filing to decision.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Once the CUA is approved (or if Planning confirms the 1996 CUA covers this use), file the Entertainment Commission application for a Place of Entertainment permit, including Police, Planning, DBI, DPH and Fire Department referrals, and post the 30-day notice at the premises. What to say: Email the Entertainment Commission Deputy Director to confirm zoning eligibility, then submit the POE application with the $2,708 fee (2026–27 schedule), a copy of the lease or the CUA approval, the business registration certificate, and proof of workers' compensation insurance. The application routes to Police, Planning, DBI, Health and Fire for review. Post the yellow notice at the premises for 30 days. Prepare an acoustic report and soundproofing plan if entertainment will be amplified. Attend the Entertainment Commission hearing (typically 45–120 days from filing) and be ready to address noise control, patron management and community concerns.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If tenant improvements are required, hire an architect to prepare plans showing the bar layout, finishes, ADA compliance, occupant load and fire exits, and submit the building permit application to DBI with Planning and Health Department plan check routing. What to say: Engage an architect licensed in California who has done San Francisco bars or restaurants. Prepare stamped plans showing the bar, seating, restrooms, ADA path of travel, occupant load calculation (for 150 capacity), and fire exits. Submit the building permit application to DBI with 'Planning' and 'Health' as routing stations. The permit application will route to Planning for zoning review (Section 175 compliance) and to DPH for approval of finishes, equipment and menu. Budget 14–120 days for plan review and $800–$15,000 in permit fees depending on construction valuation. Licensed subcontractors will pull electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Appoint a community liaison officer, register for RBS training for all alcohol servers, obtain ASCAP and BMI music licenses, and complete the health permit application with proof of a certified food safety manager on staff before opening. What to say: Before the building permit issues, appoint a community liaison (an owner, manager or designated employee) and provide written notice with name, business address and phone number to the Zoning Administrator and registered neighborhood groups. Register all bartenders and managers for California RBS training on the ABC RBS Portal ($3 registration, $10–$25 course, complete within 60 days of hire). Apply for ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses online (approximately $300–$2,500 per year each, based on occupancy and music use). File the health permit application online with the DPH at least one month before opening, with the BAN, Location ID, EIN, and proof that a certified food safety manager (ServSafe or equivalent) is on staff. Schedule the pre-opening health inspection after construction is substantially complete.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 165 to 720 days. Estimated government cost: $6,763 to $34,700. Notes: This range is the time to obtain the Conditional Use Authorization, Place of Entertainment permit and building permit with change of use when they are granted, based on catalog entries for those approvals. It does not include time to obtain the ABC license (which depends on whether beer and wine or full liquor is required) or the health permit (which is issued after final inspection). The CUA takes 120–300 days from filing to approval. The Place of Entertainment permit takes 45–120 days from filing to hearing and can be filed in parallel once the CUA is approved. The building permit takes 14–120 days for plan review and issuance. The cost range includes the CUA application fee ($3,100–$15,000), the POE application fee ($2,708), the building permit fee ($800–$15,000), the business registration certificate ($55–$700), the Fire Place of Assembly permit ($446), the sign permit ($300–$1,500), entity registration ($70–$150), seller's permit ($0), EDD registration ($0), RBS training ($3–$30 per person), ASCAP and BMI licenses ($600–$5,000 combined), and workers' compensation insurance (percentage of payroll, not a government fee). It does not include the ABC license cost: for beer and wine the application fee is $1,000–$1,600 and takes 60–150 days; for full liquor the market price for an existing license is $100,000–$450,000 and the transfer takes 90–240 days. The critical path is the CUA hearing (4–10 months), which must be approved before the Entertainment Commission will schedule the POE hearing. If the 1996 CUA conditions already permit this use, the CUA step drops out and the timeline shortens by 4–10 months, but that cannot be confirmed until Planning answers in writing.
